artists.biography:
Dutch singer Anneke van Giersbergen will forever be known as the vocalist for melancholic metallers The Gathering, but since striking out on her own in 2007, she has solidified a solo career and recorded and performed multiple times with Canadian metal genius Devin Townsend, among others.

To present her progressive metal side, Anneke formed VUUR, a new band that features some of the best heavy metal players in the Netherlands.

VUUR will release their full-length debut ‘In This Moment We Are Free - Cities’ on October 20th via InsideOut Music. From there the band will hit the road and focus on new material, as well as the heavier side of Anneke's previous outings.

perplexity.description:
In This Moment We Are Free – Cities is the debut studio album by Dutch progressive metal band VUUR, released on October 20, 2017, through Inside Out Music. The project marked a return to progressive metal for vocalist Anneke van Giersbergen, who fronts the band alongside other accomplished musicians in the genre. The album's conceptual framework centers on major world cities, with individual tracks named after locations such as Berlin, Rotterdam, and Beirut, creating a thematic journey across global urban landscapes.

The album showcases the band's commitment to complex compositional structures and technical musicianship characteristic of progressive metal. The track listing—including "My Champion - Berlin," "Time - Rotterdam," and "The Martyr And The Saint - Beirut"—demonstrates the integration of geographical references into the band's songwriting approach. This debut established VUUR's sonic identity within the progressive metal landscape, blending intricate arrangements with van Giersbergen's distinctive vocal presence.

Critical reception proved mixed upon release, with reviewers offering varied assessments of the band's debut effort. Despite the album's ambitious conceptual framework and technical proficiency, it did not achieve universal acclaim among progressive metal critics, though it succeeded in establishing VUUR as a notable entry point in the genre during 2017.
